properties.label: block-processing
properties.text: For every event in the audited mint/burn trace, check the recorded burn site is either absent or exactly equal to the single confinement site x; absence must not be encoded as a sentinel or default value, and the equality must be over the full value.
properties.assertion: forall e in tau: e.burnSite == none || e.burnSite == x (exact full-value equality; none is a genuine absence, not a sentinel)

audit_packet.guarantee: For every event of the audited trace tau, the recorded burn site is either absent (none) or exactly the single site x fixed by the burn-site confinement hypothesis. There is no third outcome and no partially matching value.
preconditions: Obligations [1]-[4], [6] (A : Type u, x : A, M : List A, tau : Trace A, e : Ev A): the audited objects are a list of mint/burn events (Trace A = List (Ev A)) over some site type A, a designated site x, and a mint-site list M. These fix the model's vocabulary; they are not implementation checks.

Obligation [5] (hc : SiteConfined M [x] tau): a caller/model precondition, not an implementation obligation. It asserts both fields at once — burn_mem (every present burn site of an event of tau is a member of the one-element list [x]) and mint_mem (every present mint site is a member of M). The conclusion below is only claimed in a state where this whole conjunction holds; the mint_mem half carries no burn-side content and is not turned into a check here.

Obligation [7] (e in tau): the conclusion ranges over membership in the single trace tau. The audited event set is exactly that trace; any event not recorded in tau is outside the guarantee, and the evidence names no particular emitting code path.

supporting_facts.claim: Under the confinement hypothesis with the singleton site list [x], every event e of tau satisfies the dichotomy e.burnSite = none OR e.burnSite = some x. These are the only two admissible outcomes.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate the events recorded in the audited trace and, for each, read the burn-site value actually stored. Compare each value against the two admissible outcomes.
supporting_facts.expected: Every recorded burn site is either absent or equal to x.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any event of the audited trace carries a present burn site that is not x.

supporting_facts.claim: sites_of_confined_singleton lifts the pointwise membership hypothesis to a conclusion universally quantified over the trace: the dichotomy holds for every member event. The statement exempts no event class, no position, and no ordering.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the burn-site value check is applied to every event of the audited trace, not to a selected subset (for example only the first such event, or only events with a nonzero amount).
supporting_facts.expected: The same none-or-exactly-x test holds for every member of the trace.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any event of the trace is exempted from the test, or the test is evaluated only on a sampled or filtered subset.

supporting_facts.claim: site_of_confined_singleton reasons on the Option value itself: the site is either genuinely none, or it is some value that requires a membership witness. Ev.burnSite is none on the mint constructor and some s on the burn constructor, so absence and presence are distinct cases, not encodings of one another.
supporting_facts.check: Inspect how the absent burn site is represented for events that record no burn. Confirm it is a real absence and not a sentinel, zero, uninitialized, or default element of A that the comparison then treats as a present, validated site.
supporting_facts.expected: Non-burning events carry an explicit absence; burning events carry a present site value.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Absence is represented by a sentinel or default element of A, or an unset field is read as if it were a present site — this collapses the two cases the evidence keeps distinct.

supporting_facts.claim: eqOfMemSingleton is an exact-equality fact: membership of b in the one-element list [x] yields Eq b x, full equality — not resemblance, not membership in a broader set, not nonzero-ness.
supporting_facts.check: Inspect the comparison used to decide that a present burn site is the confinement site. Confirm it is an exact equality over the entire value.
supporting_facts.expected: The comparison is full-value exact equality with x, with no truncation, masking, prefix or suffix matching, length-limited or lossy comparison, and no nonzero-implies-valid shortcut.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The comparison inspects fewer than all bytes of the value, normalizes or masks before comparing, or tests only that the site is nonzero or non-default — each admits a value other than x.

supporting_facts.claim: memConsElim gives exhaustive two-way elimination on a cons-list (membership in x :: l is equality with the head or membership in the tail) and notMemNil says nothing is a member of nil. For the singleton [x] the two compose to exactly one surviving case, equality with x; the tail case is discharged as impossible.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that a present burn site which is not equal to x has no admissible outcome — that the value-level case analysis leaves no additional accepted case beyond equality with x.
supporting_facts.expected: Equality with x is the only accepting case; every other present value is non-admissible.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A present burn site other than x is treated as admissible by any residual or fall-through case, so that a value the evidence rules out is recorded as a valid burn site.

derived_obligations.check: Enumerate the events of the audited trace and record each event's burn-site value; test each against the dichotomy absent-or-exactly-x.
derived_obligations.expected: Every recorded value is absent or exactly x; the enumeration covers the whole trace.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any enumerated event yields a present burn site different from x, or the enumeration does not cover every event of the trace.

derived_obligations.check: Determine the concrete representation of an absent burn site and confirm it is distinguishable from every present value.
derived_obligations.expected: Absence is represented distinctly from any element of A that could be a present site.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Absence shares a representation with a present value (sentinel, zero, default, uninitialized), so that an unvalidated value can be read as a burn site or a real site can be read as absence.

derived_obligations.check: Inspect the equality test used against x and confirm it is exact and full-value, and that no present value other than x is accepted.
derived_obligations.expected: Exact full-value equality with x is the sole accepting condition for a present burn site.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The equality is weakened (truncation, masking, nonzero test, broader membership set), or some present value other than x is accepted.

audit_packet.derivation: The root conclusion is a pointwise dichotomy over trace membership: obligation [7] (e in tau) fixes the audited event set as exactly the recorded trace, and obligation [5] (hc : SiteConfined M [x] tau) is a hypothesis supplied to the theorem, so the item checks the conclusion rather than asking the implementation to discharge the hypothesis. L001 makes the dichotomy hold for every member with no exempt class (FACT-2, OBS-1). L002 keeps absence and presence as distinct Option cases, so a sentinel must not stand in for absence (FACT-3, OBS-2). L003 supplies the strong form of the accepting case — exact equality with x, which must not be weakened — and L004 with L005 close the case analysis on the singleton so that equality with x is the only surviving case (FACT-4, FACT-5, OBS-3). Nothing in the evidence names a protocol operation, a component, an ordering, an allowlist data structure, or a configuration length, so none is asserted here.

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} (site : EthTotal.Ev A → Option A) (x : A) {τ : EthTotal.Trace A},
  (∀ (e : EthTotal.Ev A),
      List.instMembership.mem τ e →
        ∀ (d : A), Eq (site e) (Option.some d) → List.instMembership.mem (List.cons x List.nil) d) →
    ∀ (e : EthTotal.Ev A), List.instMembership.mem τ e → Or (Eq (site e) Option.none) (Eq (site e) (Option.some x))

obligations.name: h
obligations.type:
∀ (e : EthTotal.Ev A),
  List.instMembership.mem τ e →
    ∀ (d : A), Eq (site e) (Option.some d) → List.instMembership.mem (List.cons x List.nil) d
obligations.head: Membership.mem

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} {x : A} {o : Option A},
  (∀ (d : A), Eq o (Option.some d) → List.instMembership.mem (List.cons x List.nil) d) →
    Or (Eq o Option.none) (Eq o (Option.some x))

obligations.name: h
obligations.type: ∀ (d : A), Eq o (Option.some d) → List.instMembership.mem (List.cons x List.nil) d
obligations.head: Membership.mem

x_proof_closure.statement: ∀ {A : Type u} {b x : A}, List.instMembership.mem (List.cons x List.nil) b → Eq b x

∀ {A : Type u} {b x : A} {l : List A} {C : Prop},
  List.instMembership.mem (List.cons x l) b → (Eq b x → C) → (List.instMembership.mem l b → C) → C
∀ {A : Type u} {b : A}, List.instMembership.mem List.nil b → False

properties.x_fidelity_reason: Introduces client-specific components (fee burn, state.destroy_account, block processing) absent from the Lean evidence, and converts the caller-supplied hypothesis SiteConfined M [x] tau into implementation obligations (allowlist length-1, scan/branch structure, index-bounds overrun) inferred from the label and the missing_bounds_check defect class; L004/L005 are proof-internal list-induction lemmas, not statements about loop or memory bounds.

properties.label: opcodes
properties.text: Verify each account destruction zeroes the target's balance before erasing it from the live set, and that supply (the sum of balances over the live set) after n destructions plus the sum of the balances zeroed at each step equals the initial supply.
properties.assertion: zero bal then eraseLive per step ⇒ supply_n + Σ_{i<n} bal_i(a_i) = supply_0, with supply = sumOver bal live

audit_packet.guarantee: Over a chain of n account destructions, the accounting total is exactly conserved: supply after step n plus the sum of the balances each destroyed account held at the moment of its destruction equals the initial supply. No step may create, lose, or double-count value beyond the balance actually removed. The theorem is stated over an abstract Ledger (live list + balance map) with a destruction modelled as setBal a 0 followed by eraseLive a; it names no opcode, block, or client.
preconditions: Model hypothesis (not an implementation obligation) hmem: at every step i the destruction target a_i is a member of (Ls i).live. The theorem says nothing about what happens when this fails.

Model hypothesis (not an implementation obligation) hnext: supply (Ls (i+1)) equals the supply of ((Ls i).setBal (a_i) 0).eraseLive (a_i). The conclusion applies only to chains whose successor supply is pinned to this canonical two-part destruction; an implementation whose destruction path differs falls outside the theorem rather than contradicting it.
Structural invariants carried by every Ledger value: live is Distinct (no duplicate entries) and bal_live (any account with nonzero balance is in live).
Supply is defined as sumOver bal live — the sum of balances over exactly the live list, not an independently maintained counter.
Balances are Nat; the account type A only needs DecidableEq.

supporting_facts.claim: Chain conservation: for every n, supply(state n) + sumOver (fun i => bal_i(a_i)) (range n) = supply(state 0). Exact equality over the whole chain, not per-step-only and not approximate.
supporting_facts.check: Instrument a run of consecutive destructions: record supply before the first, each target's balance at the instant of its destruction, and supply after the last.
supporting_facts.expected: final_supply + sum_of_recorded_destroyed_balances == initial_supply, exactly, with no tolerance.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The equality fails in either direction for some n, or the implementation only enforces a weaker property (supply non-increasing, supply nonzero, or supply changed approximately by the destroyed balance).

supporting_facts.claim: Single-step exactness (supply_destroy): supply((setBal a 0 ha).eraseLive a) + bal(a) = supply(L). One destruction reduces the total by exactly the target's prior balance — no more, no less.
supporting_facts.check: For each individual destruction, compare supply before and after that single step against the target's balance immediately before the step.
supporting_facts.expected: supply_after + bal_before(a) == supply_before for every destruction, including when bal_before(a) == 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A single destruction changes supply by an amount other than the target's prior balance, or a zero-balance destruction changes supply at all.

supporting_facts.claim: The zeroing move is exact (supply_setBal_zero: supply(setBal a 0) + bal(a) = supply(L); general form supply_setBal: supply(setBal a v) + bal(a) = supply(L) + v). The debit is exactly the old balance and the credit exactly the written value.
supporting_facts.check: Isolate the balance-write half of destruction and compare the supply delta against the account's old balance (and, for the general write path, the newly written value).
supporting_facts.expected: Supply drops by exactly the old balance when the write is 0; for a general write, supply + old == supply_before + new.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The write leaves stale value in the total, double-subtracts the old balance, or the total is adjusted by anything other than old/new balance.

supporting_facts.claim: Removal is supply-neutral (supply_eraseLive, sumOver_eraseOne_of_zero, sumOver_eraseOneOfPoint_of_zero): erasing an entry from the live list leaves supply unchanged — the zero-balance precondition is what makes erasure safe.
supporting_facts.check: Verify erasure from the live set only occurs after the balance is zero, and measure the supply delta across the erasure step alone.
supporting_facts.expected: supply_after_removal == supply_before_removal exactly, and the removed account's balance is 0 at removal time.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An entry is erased from live while still holding a nonzero balance (that value silently leaves the total), or erasure alters supply at all.

supporting_facts.claim: The destroy guard is an exact equality (destroy_guard, setBal_bal_self, setBalOfPoint_bal_self): after setBal a 0 on a live account, reading a's balance back yields exactly 0 — the value written is the value observed.
supporting_facts.check: After the zeroing step and before erasure, read the target's balance back through the same accessor the erasure step uses.
supporting_facts.expected: read_back_balance(a) == 0 exactly.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The read-back is nonzero, is served from a different view of state than the erasure step consults, or the zero is assumed rather than observed before erasure proceeds.

supporting_facts.claim: Telescoping is valid (supply_acc_chain): if supply(i+1) + b_i = supply(i) + m_i holds at every index i, then supply(n) + sumOver b (range n) = supply(0) + sumOver m (range n). The chain result follows only from a per-step relation holding at EVERY index without exception.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the per-step supply relation is enforced at every destruction in the sequence — not sampled, not exempted for edge cases (same account destroyed twice, self-targeted destruction, destruction of a just-created account).
supporting_facts.expected: The per-step relation holds at every index i; no step is exempt.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any step bypasses per-step accounting (e.g. deferred or batched destruction reconciled only at the end), which would let an intermediate violation be cancelled by another.

supporting_facts.claim: No residual credit (sumOver_zero): the credit side of the telescope is sumOver (fun _ => 0) = 0 exactly, so the destruction chain contributes no offsetting creation to the total.
supporting_facts.check: Verify the destruction path carries no compensating credit — no supply increment, refund into the total, or rebalancing that offsets the removed balance.
supporting_facts.expected: The credit term over the chain is exactly 0; the total accounts only for removed balances.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Destruction is paired with a supply-increasing effect that makes the total look conserved while value was in fact created.

supporting_facts.claim: The update identity needs distinctness and membership (sumOver_update / sumOver_updateOfPoint): sumOver (fun b => if b = a then v else f b) l + f a = sumOver f l + v holds only for a Distinct list l containing a.
supporting_facts.check: Check that the live list cannot hold duplicate entries for one account, and that the target is present in live before the balance write is applied.
supporting_facts.expected: live is duplicate-free at every step; presence of the target is established, not assumed.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account can appear twice in the live list (its balance is counted twice and the write repairs only one occurrence), or the identity is relied on for a write to a non-member.

supporting_facts.claim: No collateral effect (sumOver_update_notMemOfPoint): updating an account absent from a list leaves that list's sum completely unchanged — destroying a_i must not perturb any other account's contribution.
supporting_facts.check: Diff the full balance map and live list across a single destruction step.
supporting_facts.expected: Only the target's balance and its live entry change; every other account's balance and contribution to supply is identical before and after.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any account other than the target has its balance or supply contribution altered by the destruction.

derived_obligations.check: Enforce the ordering: the balance write to 0 strictly precedes removal from the live list, and removal is gated on the observed zero balance rather than on an assumption.
derived_obligations.expected: Every destruction executes set-balance-to-0, then read-back == 0, then erase-from-live, in that order.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Removal happens first, the two steps are reordered or interleaved under any condition, or the zero-balance gate is elided.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the exact per-step supply relation across every destruction, and the accumulated relation across the whole sequence.
derived_obligations.expected: supply_after + destroyed_balance == supply_before at each step; supply_end + Σ destroyed_balances == supply_start over the sequence.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Only an aggregate end-of-sequence reconciliation exists that could mask offsetting per-step errors, or the check tolerates a nonzero delta.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm supply is derived from the live list and balance map (sumOver bal live) rather than tracked as an independent counter that can drift from the state it summarizes.
derived_obligations.expected: Supply is recomputable from state, and any cached total matches the recomputed sum at every step.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A cached or incrementally maintained total can diverge from the sum of balances over the live list.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the live list holds no duplicate entries at any point, including after erasure (erasure removes a single occurrence).
derived_obligations.expected: Distinctness of live is preserved by both the balance write and the erasure.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A duplicate live entry survives an erasure, so a destroyed account's balance remains counted in the total.

audit_packet.derivation: The root conclusion (FACT-1) is obtained by telescoping (FACT-6, supply_acc_chain) a per-step conservation fact. That per-step fact is supply_destroy (FACT-2), which splits a destruction into two exact accounting moves: the write of 0 debits supply by exactly the old balance (FACT-3, resting on the exact update identity FACT-8, which needs a Distinct live list containing the target), and erasing the now-zero entry is supply-neutral (FACT-4). The bridge between the two moves is the destroy guard (FACT-5): setBal a 0 provably reads back as exactly 0, which is precisely the precondition eraseLive demands. FACT-9 confirms the write touches no other account, and FACT-7 collapses the credit side of the telescope to exactly 0 so the chain identity has no minted residue. hmem and hnext are hypotheses of the theorem, not implementation obligations: they delimit the chains the conclusion covers (targets are live; successor supply is pinned to this canonical two-part destruction). The falsifiable checks above are OBS-1..OBS-4, all recoverable from the conclusion and the DAG lemmas without assuming any particular opcode, block structure, or client architecture.

omitted_facts.reason: EthTotal.notMemNil (membership in the empty list is absurd) is a base-case eliminator inside list induction; it carries no implementation-observable accounting content beyond the distinctness/membership content already captured in FACT-8 and OBS-4.

EthTotal.memConsElim is a case-split eliminator for membership in a cons-list, induction plumbing for the sumOver update proof; its content is already exposed as the membership side condition in FACT-8.

properties.x_fidelity_reason: The item and packet bind an abstract Ledger destruction chain to SELFDESTRUCT, block processing, and cross-client consensus — none of which appear in the theorem (inferred from the `opcodes` label and defect class) — and promote the caller hypotheses hmem/hnext into implementation obligations (OBS-1/OBS-2/OBS-3).

properties.label: state-trie
properties.text: Verify a balance-only ledger update conserves the total exactly: with the live account set unchanged and each live account enumerated once, confirm post-total plus total decreases equals pre-total plus total increases, deltas truncating on unsigned balances.
properties.assertion: live'==live && distinct(live) && (bal!=0 -> a in live) && supply' + Σ_live(bal-bal') == supply + Σ_live(bal'-bal)

audit_packet.guarantee: For any two ledger states L (pre) and L' (post) sharing the same enumerated live account list, the total is exactly reconciled by the per-account deltas: L'.supply + Σ_{a∈L.live}(L.bal a − L'.bal a) = L.supply + Σ_{a∈L.live}(L'.bal a − L.bal a), where supply is defined as the sum of balances folded over the live list and subtraction is truncating on unsigned (Nat) balances. Equivalently: total credits minus total debits accounts for every unit of change in the total — no balance write can create or destroy total that is not matched by an opposite recorded delta.
preconditions: hlive (root obligation [4]): the post-state's enumerated live account list is the same list as the pre-state's — the update under audit changes balances only, and does not add, drop, or otherwise alter the enumerated account set. This is a caller-side applicability condition: the identity may only be relied on for transitions that satisfy it.
dl (obligation of L001, discharged in the model by Ledger.live_distinct): the live account list is duplicate-free; enumeration yields each account at most once.

hcov (obligation of L001, discharged in the model by Ledger.bal_live on L): every pre-state account with a nonzero balance is a member of the enumerated live list — no nonzero balance exists outside the enumerated set.

hcov' (obligation of L001, discharged in the model by Ledger.bal_live on L', transported along hlive): every post-state account with a nonzero balance is likewise a member of that same enumerated list.

Balances inhabit the unsigned naturals (Ledger.bal : A → Nat) and subtraction is truncating (x − y = 0 when x ≤ y); supply is Ledger.supply = sumOver bal live, i.e. recomputed by folding balances over the live list, not read from an independently maintained counter. Obligations [1]-[3] fix the account type A and the two ledger states and carry no implementation content.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact total conservation (equality, not a bound): with the live list unchanged, post-total plus the sum of all per-account decreases equals pre-total plus the sum of all per-account increases. L001 proves this for any duplicate-free list that covers the nonzero-balance support of both states; the root instantiates it at L.live.
supporting_facts.check: For a state transition that only writes balances, compute the pre-state total by enumerating every live account and summing balances; do the same for the post state; independently accumulate, per touched account, the decrease (pre − post) and the increase (post − pre). Compare post_total + Σdecreases against pre_total + Σincreases.
supporting_facts.expected: The two sides are exactly equal, for every such transition, with no tolerance and no rounding slack.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The two sides differ by any amount; or the implementation reports or persists a total that is not equal to the freshly recomputed fold over the live list; or the equality holds only for the accounts the code believes it touched while a second write path mutated a balance without contributing to either delta accumulator.

supporting_facts.claim: The total is a function of the balance support, not of the list representation or enumeration order: two duplicate-free lists whose membership agrees on every account with a nonzero balance produce identical sums (L002), and pointwise-equal balance functions produce identical sums (L004, L006 — agreement needed only on members of the list).
supporting_facts.check: Recompute the total from two different enumerations of the same state (e.g. the live list in a different order, or a second independent enumeration path), and recompute it after any representation change that leaves every account's balance unchanged.
supporting_facts.expected: Every enumeration of the same underlying state yields the same total; accounts whose balances are untouched contribute identically before and after.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The computed total depends on enumeration order or on the internal representation of the account collection; or an untouched account's contribution to the total changes across the transition.

supporting_facts.claim: Distinctness is preserved and membership is stable under extraction of a single account: a distinct list splits as l₁ ++ (a :: l₂) around any member (L010), the account then does not occur in l₁ ++ l₂ (L013), that remainder stays distinct (L014), and every other account's membership is preserved in both directions by removing or re-inserting a (L011, L012).
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the enumeration used to compute the total emits each account at most once — no account is reached through two paths, and no account is skipped when a sibling account is updated. Exercise updates that touch an account at the head, the middle, and the tail of the enumeration.
supporting_facts.expected: Each account appears exactly once per enumeration; removing one account from the enumeration leaves every other account present exactly once.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account is enumerated twice (its balance is double-counted into the total) or an account with a nonzero balance is missed by enumeration (its balance vanishes from the total); or writing one account's balance perturbs the enumeration multiplicity of another.

supporting_facts.claim: Sums decompose exactly: the sum over a concatenation is the sum of the parts (L018), pulling one account out of the middle contributes exactly its own balance plus the sum of the rest (L015), and a pointwise sum of two balance functions splits into the sum of their totals (L003). Together these make the total's delta for a single balance write exactly that account's own delta.
supporting_facts.check: For a transition touching a known set of accounts, compare an incrementally maintained total (pre-total adjusted by each write's own delta) against a full re-enumeration of every live account in the post state; also verify that partitioning the live list and summing the parts reproduces the whole.
supporting_facts.expected: Incremental adjustment and full recomputation agree exactly; the change in the total equals the sum of the individual per-account deltas and nothing else.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Writing one account's balance moves the total by an amount other than that account's own delta; or partitioned sums do not add up to the full-enumeration total; or an incremental total counter drifts from a full recomputation.

supporting_facts.claim: Truncating-subtraction symmetry underpins the reconciliation: x + (y − x) = y + (x − y) on unsigned balances (L005), justified by x ≤ y ⇒ x + (y − x) = y (L016) and x ≤ y ⇒ x − y = 0 (L017). A decrease is therefore recorded on the debit side and contributes exactly zero to the credit side, and vice versa.
supporting_facts.check: For each touched account, compute both directions of the delta (pre − post and post − pre) under the implementation's unsigned balance arithmetic, covering pre < post, pre > post, pre = post, and balances at the extremes of the representable range.
supporting_facts.expected: Exactly one direction is nonzero and equals the true magnitude of the change; the other is exactly zero — matching truncating (saturating-at-zero) semantics.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An unsigned subtraction departs from truncating semantics (wrapping to a near-maximal value, or a balance going below zero); a debit is clamped so the corresponding credit is unmatched; or a delta is computed against a stale pre-balance so both directions are wrong while their difference still looks plausible.

supporting_facts.claim: Zero contributions are genuinely zero: the sum of the constant-zero function over any list is 0 (L008) and nothing is a member of the empty list (L007). Combined with the hcov/hcov' preconditions, an account outside the enumeration must carry balance zero and contributes nothing to the total.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that zero-balance accounts — including accounts absent from the enumeration — contribute nothing to the total, that an empty live list yields total zero, and that any account not present in the enumeration reads as balance zero.
supporting_facts.expected: Zero-balance and non-enumerated accounts contribute exactly 0; adding or removing a zero-balance account leaves the total unchanged.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A non-enumerated account can hold a nonzero balance (breaking hcov/hcov' and hiding value from the total); or adding/removing a zero-balance account shifts the total; or an absent account is treated as anything other than balance zero.

derived_obligations.check: After every batch of balance writes, recompute the total by full enumeration over the post state and reconcile it against the pre-state total using the two-sided identity post_total + Σdebits = pre_total + Σcredits, where debits and credits are accumulated per account at write time.
derived_obligations.expected: Exact equality on every transition, including transitions that write the same account more than once and transitions that write a balance to its existing value.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any transition where the identity fails, or where a balance write path exists that does not feed the delta accumulators.

derived_obligations.check: Assert that the enumeration used to compute the total visits each live account exactly once and that the computed total is invariant across independent enumerations of the same state.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any account visited twice or skipped, or a total that varies with enumeration order or with the internal representation of the account collection.

derived_obligations.check: Before relying on the identity, confirm the transition actually satisfies the modeled precondition hlive: the enumerated live account list is identical pre and post, and no account outside it holds a nonzero balance in either state. Transitions that change the enumerated set are outside this theorem's scope and must be reconciled separately.
derived_obligations.expected: Identical enumerated account list pre and post; no nonzero balance outside it.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A balance write implicitly adds, removes, or hides an account from the enumeration, or a nonzero balance persists in an account unreachable by enumeration — in either case the total changes without a matching recorded delta and the identity no longer applies.

derived_obligations.check: Check every balance delta computation against the truncating-unsigned model: compute decrease and increase as saturating differences and assert that at most one is nonzero and that its magnitude matches the actual pre/post balance change.
derived_obligations.expected: Truncating semantics with a matched, non-wrapping magnitude on exactly one side.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A subtraction that wraps instead of truncating, a clamped debit without a compensating credit, or a delta computed from a stale pre-balance.

derived_obligations.check: Assert that reading an account absent from the enumeration yields balance zero, and that adding or removing zero-balance accounts leaves the total unchanged.
derived_obligations.expected: Zero-balance accounts are total-neutral; an empty live list totals zero.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A default or missing account resolves to a nonzero balance, or adding/removing a zero-balance account shifts the total.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem exact_supply is obtained by instantiating exact_supply_on (L001) at the list L.live: its three obligations are discharged by the Ledger structure invariants — live_distinct supplies dl, bal_live supplies hcov, and bal_live on L' transported along the root obligation hlive (L'.live = L.live) supplies hcov'. L001 in turn combines four ingredients: sumOver_eq_of_support_iff (L002) shows the total depends only on the nonzero-balance support and not on the list representation, itself built from the distinctness/membership plumbing (L010–L014) and the sum decomposition lemmas (L015, L018, L008, L007, L009); sumOver_add (L003) splits sums of pointwise-added functions; sumOver_congr (L004, via L006) replaces balance functions that agree on members; and add_sub_symm (L005), justified by add_sub_cancel_of_le (L016) and sub_eq_zero_of_le (L017), supplies the per-account truncating-subtraction symmetry x + (y − x) = y + (x − y) that makes each account's contribution reconcile exactly on both sides. The packet mirrors this structure: FACT-1 carries the root equality, FACT-2/FACT-3 carry the enumeration-integrity facts that make the total well-defined, FACT-4 carries exact decomposition (so one write moves the total by exactly its own delta), FACT-5 carries unsigned-arithmetic safety, and FACT-6 carries the zero/coverage boundary. Preconditions retain all root must-establish obligations (hlive plus the dl/hcov/hcov' obligations inherited from L001), stated as model-side conditions rather than as facts proved about any implementation. No component, operation, or data structure beyond the Ledger's live list and Nat-valued balance function is referenced.

omitted_facts.reason: memConsElim is pure case-analysis plumbing for list membership (a member of x :: l is either the head or in the tail). It introduces no security-relevant claim of its own beyond the distinctness and membership-stability facts already carried by FACT-3, and it is consumed only internally by L002.
